newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PEARCE'S ASSISTANT QUITS TROUBLED FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEARCE'S ASSISTANT QUITS TROUBLED FOREST.

text.p: Nottingham Forest's off-field wrangling continued on Tuesday when assistant manager Alan Hill quit the English premier league side to join his former boss Frank Clark at Manchester City.

Hill was angry at the rejection by shareholders of a bid by a consortium to gain power at a shareholders meeting on Monday. The failure of the bid means there will be at least a further three weeks' uncertainty at the City Ground before a new bid is launched by a different consortium.

"I have got a mortgage, I have a family to keep and I need the work, and Manchester City have offered me that opportunity," Hill said. "I got the impression I was being lined up for the sack and I did not want that to happen."

Hill's departure could pave the way for an extension of the Clough dynasty at Forest. Caretaker-manager and player Stuart Pearce is said to be ready to install Nigel Clough, son of Brian, as his new assistant.
Clough junior is currently on-loan from Manchester City, now under the managership of former Forest manager Clark, who walked out of the City Ground last month.
But on Tuesday Pearce rejected the idea of a swap deal which would have brought Clough on a permanent basis in exchange for Forest goalkeeper Tommy Wright and defender Des Lyttle.

It now seems Pearce will be unable to buy Clough until at least the end of this month when another consortium, headed by property millionaire Nigel Wray, will launch the latest formal bid to take control of the club.
If the bid is successful it could provide Pearce with money to bolster his side, currently second bottom of the premier league.
Brian Clough managed Forest from 1975 to 1993.
